references.text: Continues the theme of circumcision as a sign of the covenant between God and Abraham's descendants.
Refers to the fulfillment of God's command regarding circumcision with Isaac.
Circumcision is mentioned as part of the law given to the children of Israel.
Joshua circumcises the Israelites in accordance with the covenant command given to Abraham.
Jesus notes that circumcision came from the fathers (Abraham) and links it to the Law of Moses.
Stephen refers to the covenant with Abraham, including circumcision.
Paul discusses the significance of circumcision as a sign and seal of the righteousness Abraham had by faith.
Paul emphasizes that in Christ neither circumcision nor uncircumcision matters, but faith working through love.
Contrast between God's holy covenant requirements and human manipulation of the same sign.
Theological parallel between the covenant with Noah and the covenant with Abraham, both sharing the structure 'with you and your descendants'.
Direct contextual connection: The promise in 17:4 requires the sign in 17:10 to be upheld.
Parallel between the signs of the covenants (rainbow vs. circumcision) confirming God's eternal promises.
Direct linguistic and theological parallel between the covenants with Noah and Abraham regarding 'you and your descendants'.
Theological contrast: Circumcision as a covenant requirement (OT) versus warning against circumcision as a requirement for salvation (NT).
Theological development: From an external sign (circumcision) to inner cleansing (water) in God's plan.
Direct connection through the covenant formula 'my people and their God' as the center of both texts.
Theological context: The covenant is established (Gen 17:10) and restored (Ezek 36:28) with the same formula.
Principle and specification: Circumcision as part of 'living by' God's laws.
Theological contrast: The covenant with a sign (circumcision) versus the new covenant with forgiveness of sins.
Circumcision as a fundamental covenant requirement to be able to keep 'all' of God's laws.
Circumcision as the covenant requirement that initiates life in God's laws.
The principle of exact observance of God's commands illustrated through the covenant of circumcision.
The covenant (circumcision) as a prerequisite for being clean and belonging to the holy.
Circumcision as the covenant basis for living in the land as God's people.
The covenant (circumcision) defines the people; obedience ensures security in the land.
The covenant formula links circumcision (sign) and obedience (lifestyle) to the relationship with God.
Parallel between two different covenants (Noah and Abraham), both being eternal promises from God.
Contrast: The covenant holds the people together; breaking the covenant leads to scattering.
